hub-hf.d: Service that hosts models as git repositories (with Git LFS for large files). A checkpoint is a commit of that repository: a fixed set of files.

git-lfs.d: Git extension for large files: the repository stores only a pointer with the SHA-256 of the content, and the bytes live in separate storage. Weight shards are LFS files.

generation-config.d: The checkpoint's sampling defaults (temperature, top_p, top_k, eos), used by vLLM when the client doesn't send values; --generation-config vllm ignores it.

trust-remote-code.d: Allows the engine to run Python code shipped in the model repository (custom architectures or encoders). Because it is executed code, it should come from a pinned revision.

safetensors.d: Weight format with no executable code: 8 bytes holding the header size N, N bytes of JSON (dtype, shape and data_offsets of each tensor) and the raw bytes. Enables mmap, zero-copy and partial reads.

shard-checkpoint.d: Each of the .safetensors files a large checkpoint is split into, to allow parallel downloads, resuming and piece-by-piece verification.

weight-map.d: Map, inside model.safetensors.index.json, from each tensor name to the shard that contains it. It defines what a complete snapshot is.

mmap.d: Mapping a file into virtual memory: the operating system only reads from disk the pages that are actually touched (page faults), with no intermediate copy.

zero-copy.d: Using the bytes where they already are (for example, in a mapped page of the file) instead of copying them into another buffer before use.

range-read.d: Partial read of a remote file via the HTTP header Range: bytes=a-b. With safetensors you can fetch just the header and just the tensors you want.

weight-loader.d: Function attached to each vLLM parameter that copies a checkpoint tensor into it, cutting out the rank's slice (TP/EP) and the right slot (shard_id).

weights-mapper.d: Table of rules (prefixes, suffixes, substrings, regex) that translates checkpoint tensor names into vLLM parameter names.

stacked-params.d: A fused parameter that receives several checkpoint tensors into slots (shard_id), such as gate_proj + up_proj → gate_up_proj: one bigger GEMM instead of several small ones.

tensor-parallel.d: Splitting each matrix across GPUs. Since PyTorch stores W as [out, in], column-parallel cuts the rows of W (the outputs, with no communication) and row-parallel cuts the columns (the inputs, with an all-reduce of the partial sums). Each rank loads only its own slice; for a quantized weight, the scales are cut along with it.

quantization-config.d: Block of config.json that says how to interpret the quantized bytes: method, per-layer algorithm, group sizes, excluded modules.

quant-method.d: Field of quantization_config that vLLM uses to pick the class responsible for the checkpoint (e.g. exl3, modelopt).

quantized-layers.d: In ModelOpt MIXED_PRECISION, a map from module prefix → {quant_algo, group_size}. Matching is by exact string: a different prefix leaves the layer unquantized.

config-groups.d: compressed-tensors-style quantization groups, with targets (name patterns) and weights.num_bits. In Qwen's nvidia checkpoint, it is the only place that declares the PLE as FP8.

hf-quant-config.d: ModelOpt's legacy sidecar with the quantization metadata. It can disagree with config.json, and different parts of vLLM read each one.

text-config.d: The language model's sub-config inside the config of a multimodal model (next to vision_config). It is the one the LLM reads.

preflight.d: A quick check run before a long operation (such as loading the weights), so it fails in seconds instead of minutes.

blob-hf.d: File in blobs/ of the Hugging Face cache, named by the hash of its content (SHA-256 for LFS, git blob SHA-1 for small files). Stored only once, even if several revisions use it.

snapshot-hf.d: The snapshots/<commit>/ directory with relative symlinks to the blobs, assembling the view of one commit of the repository.

refs-main.d: Text file in the HF cache holding the hash of the commit that main pointed to. In offline mode, resolving main means reading this file; an extra newline can break the resolution.

modo-offline-hf.d: With HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 (and TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1), the library doesn't touch the network and resolves everything from the local cache: a reproducible boot, with no surprise downloads.

hard-link.d: A second directory entry for the same file (same inode): not a single byte is copied. It must point to the real blob, not to a relative symlink.

revisao-pinada.d: Serving a model by the immutable hash of a commit (40 hex) instead of a moving pointer like main, so the bytes never change without notice.

espelho-checkpoint.d: A byte-identical copy of a model repository in a repository you control, to survive changes to, or the removal of, the upstream.

repo-gated.d: A Hub repository that requires accepting terms on its page and authenticating with HF_TOKEN; without that, the download returns HTTP 403.

fail-closed.d: The policy of refusing the operation when a check fails (hash, count, header), instead of carrying on in degraded mode.

sha-256.d: A 256-bit cryptographic hash function. Flipping a single bit of the input changes about half of the output bits (avalanche effect); it is the lfs.oid that the Hub publishes for LFS files.

git-blob-sha1.d: The identifier git assigns to a file: SHA1("blob " + size + "\0" + content). It is the oid the Hub publishes for small (non-LFS) files.

checkpoint-derivado.d: A checkpoint built locally from pinned inputs (by converting, overlaying or transplanting tensors), verified before serving and kept in its own local repository.

rsync.d: Tool that synchronizes directories by copying only what differs. Used to give the worker a local copy of the weights.

nfs.d: Network File System: one node exports a directory and another mounts it over the network. In the recipes, the head exports the HF cache read-only (NFSv4.2, nconnect=8) and the worker reads through it.

connectx-7.d: NVIDIA network card found in the DGX Spark. In the recipes, its 200 Gb/s QSFP ports connect the two nodes directly: NCCL (RDMA) and the rsync or NFS of the weights both go through them.

xet-hf.d: The Hub's storage and transfer backend that splits files into content-addressed chunks, deduplicated across versions, replacing the classic LFS transport. HF_HUB_DISABLE_XET=1 falls back to whole-file HTTP downloads.

quantizacao-na-carga.d: Quantizing the weights at the moment the engine loads them, instead of writing a derived checkpoint: the disk keeps the published checkpoint (for example, dense weights in BF16) and the GPU gets the quantized version (the DENSE=q4 of the GLM TensorFold version). It saves one artifact to build, pin and verify, but the served bytes have no hash on disk and the conversion is repeated on every boot.
